title: Dutch firm uses AI to help drone systems 'talk' on Ukraine's battlefield
source_used: Arise News, which carries the Reuters report (Reuters original returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: Dutch company Intelic is developing AI software, Nexus, that connects different drone, radar and air-defence systems; it is now being deployed in Ukraine.
Intelic has a €30 million contract with the Dutch Defence Ministry to upgrade the country's air defences and an office in Kyiv.

In a late-September test at a former Dutch airbase, Nexus combined radar, sensor and camera data and a drone verified the target, but a human operator made the final decision to launch the interceptor.
Intelic's CEO Maurits Korthals Altes said the process could eventually become fully autonomous.
Intelic says Europe has over 700 drone makers whose systems do not always talk to each other.
The software supplements Delta, Ukraine's own battlefield management platform.
Intelic says automation could cut minutes between detecting and trying to intercept a drone.
quote_evidence: Amsterdam-based Intelic has a €30 million ($33.5 million) contract with the Dutch Defence Ministry to upgrade the country’s air defences.
A human operator made the final decision to launch the interceptor during the test, but Intelic CEO and founder Maurits Korthals Altes said the process could eventually become fully autonomous.
Intelic’s command-and-control system is now being rolled out in Ukraine, where some operational decisions are still communicated through chat applications or phone calls.
why_it_matters_hint: Linking different makers' drones and sensors could speed up responses to attacks, with a human still deciding for now.
notes: Reuters page blocked; text read on Arise News, which matches the Reuters story's subject and quotes but whose wording we could not compare with Reuters'. Company claims on speed are Intelic's own.
